summary: Keep the spatial curve and its projected diagram in one scene, so a crossing count belongs to the projection and not to the knot.
objective: Build a trefoil where I can rotate the projection direction, count crossings in the shadow diagram and see that the tabulated crossing number is a minimum, not a picture property.
intent_signals: Show the difference between a knot and one of its diagrams.
Explain why a knot has a minimum crossing number.
example_prompts: Build a trefoil knot with a projected diagram whose crossings I can count as I rotate the projection.
Show a deformed trefoil that still has the same tabulated invariants.
negative_signals: Not a knot classification tool: this recipe does not compute invariants from arbitrary user curves.
Not a rope or physical cord simulation; no contact, friction or thickness dynamics.
not_for: Not a knot classification tool: this recipe does not compute invariants from arbitrary user curves.
Not a rope or physical cord simulation; no contact, friction or thickness dynamics.

entities.name: Space curve
entities.guidance: Build the knot as a closed tube along a parametrised curve with no self-intersection at the modelled radius.

entities.name: Projection diagram
entities.guidance: Draw a diagram on a plane with explicit over and under breaks at crossings, generated from the current projection direction.

entities.name: Crossing markers
entities.guidance: Mark each crossing in the diagram with its sign and let the count be displayed, since a bad projection direction can create degenerate tangencies.

state_contract.model: A parametrised closed curve, a projection direction, a computed crossing set with over and under assignment, and a tabulated invariant record shown as reference data rather than as a computed result.
state_contract.authority: The space curve is authoritative for the knot; the diagram is derived from the projection direction, and any deformation control must preserve the curve being embedded.
actions: Rotate the projection direction and recount crossings.
Deform the curve within an authored isotopy and confirm the tabulated invariants are unchanged.
Toggle the tube, the centreline and the diagram plane.
Reset the curve and the projection.

invariants: The tube never self-intersects; a deformation that would pinch it is rejected rather than rendered.
The displayed crossing count is a property of the current projection and can exceed the tabulated crossing number.

Non-generic projections are reported as invalid diagrams rather than counted: tangencies, triple crossings and crossings that coincide with the projection of a vertex all invalidate the diagram, and the minimum-crossing comparison applies only to valid generic diagrams.
motion_guidance: Animate deformations slowly so the viewer can see that no strand passes through another.

Rotate the projection direction continuously and recompute crossing locations and over-under data every time. The count itself changes only at transitions between generic projections, so an unchanged count over a small rotation is expected rather than evidence of a stale diagram.
known_limits: Tabulated invariants are displayed as reference data from a knot table, not computed by the scene.
Mirror and orientation conventions differ between tables, so handedness is not asserted here.
Authored guidance only: no scene runtime, rendering or numerical calibration has been run for this recipe.

claims.statement: The trefoil is tabulated as knot 3_1 with crossing number 3, and its entry lists an Alexander polynomial and a Jones polynomial.
claims.scope: Reference-table data for the catalogued knot as displayed; polynomial normalisation and mirror conventions vary between tables, so the scene should show the values as quoted from its chosen table.

object_craft.structure: Swept tube with enough radial segments that the over and under passes stay round where strands come close.
object_craft.material: Matte tube with a length-varying stripe so the traversal direction and any twist are visible during deformation.
object_craft.articulation: The curve is deformed by control points; the tube is rebuilt from the curve each time.

object_craft.structure: Flat strokes with real gaps at under-strands, drawn on a bounded plane with a visible border.
object_craft.material: High-contrast strokes on a plain plate; the diagram must stay readable when the 3D tube is behind it.
object_craft.articulation: Regenerated whenever the projection direction or the curve changes.

physical_contract.scope: Authored deformation of a curve and projection; no rope physics or self-collision solving.
checks: No self-intersection at the modelled tube radius during any authored deformation.

Recompute crossing locations and over-under data after projection changes; a small generic change may preserve the count. Compare against the tabulated minimum only for valid generic diagrams, and report nongeneric projections as invalid.
